records.claim_text: The Project Information System is the umbrella reporting component used to monitor and control project data, covering single projects, partial projects, or multiple projects at once.
records.evidence_quote: The Project Information System is a flexible, comprehensive information system you can use to monitor and control your project data.

records.claim_text: Standard project reporting spans five families: Structures, Controlling, Progress, Resources and Material, each offered at differing degrees of detail and summarization.
records.evidence_quote: The standard also includes reports offering different degrees of detail, summarizations, and views of current data, version data, and archive data

records.topic: Drill to source document - documented expectation
records.claim_text: Official guidance routes the user need 'trace the origin of your costs at document level' to CO line item reports, establishing document-level traceability as a first-class reporting requirement.
records.evidence_quote: Trace the origin of your costs at document level

records.claim_text: A hierarchical overview of cost and payment data is served by hierarchy reports, not by cost element or line item reports.
records.evidence_quote: View a hierarchical overview of your cost and payment data

records.topic: Report type selection - cost element view
records.claim_text: Detail at cost element level is served by a distinct report family (cost element reports), separate from hierarchy reports.
records.evidence_quote: Evaluate detailed information at cost element level

records.claim_text: Project information system data can be transferred to a separate business warehouse for management reporting, i.e. the operational info system is not the only consumption layer.
records.evidence_quote: You can transfer data from the project information system to the SAP Business Information Warehouse (BW).

records.claim_text: Hierarchy reports do not read transactional tables directly; they evaluate a dedicated summarized project information database.
records.evidence_quote: The evaluation is based on all the data in the RPSCO project information database.

records.claim_text: Hierarchy reporting aggregates by value category, which is a grouping of cost elements and commitment items - a reporting dimension distinct from the GL account.
records.evidence_quote: RPSCO contains all project-related cost, revenue, and payment data, summarized by value category. Value categories are groupings of cost elements and commitment items.

records.topic: Budget vs commitment vs actual vs assigned
records.claim_text: The canonical project control comparison delivered as a report definition example is plan versus actual versus commitment versus assigned values on one row set.
records.evidence_quote: The text that follows contains an example of defining a report, in which you can compare plan, actual, commitment, and assigned values.

records.claim_text: Which value types (plan, actual, budget) appear in a project report is defined in a reusable form object, not hard-coded per report.
records.evidence_quote: you define the value types to be displayed in a report, for example, the plan, actual, and/or budget values.

records.claim_text: Hierarchy reports return correct figures only if cost elements and commitment items have been assigned to value categories beforehand; a checking program verifies the assignment.
records.evidence_quote: For the system to be able to evaluate data correctly in the hierarchy reports, you must assign the cost elements and commitment items

records.claim_text: The summarized project information database must be reconstructed on first report access and whenever value categories change - a rebuild step, not a live view.
records.evidence_quote: You must reconstruct the project information database when you first access the report and when you subsequently change any of the value categories.

records.claim_text: Project value reporting is evaluated within a single controlling area, which fixes the reporting currency and fiscal year variant for the whole report.
records.evidence_quote: Evaluation is within a controlling area. The controlling area determines which currency and fiscal year variant are used.

records.claim_text: A report/report interface lets a hierarchy report call up further reports, and the permitted branch targets are declared as configuration parameters.
records.evidence_quote: You can use the report/report interface to call up more reports. You can branch to the following types of report:

records.claim_text: Report-to-report navigation targets are maintained by a copy function in configuration and must be re-maintained whenever new reports are defined.
records.evidence_quote: You maintain the report/report interface parameters using a copy function in the Project System IMG.

records.topic: Drill from total to source document
records.claim_text: From a project line item report the user can branch to the corresponding source document, completing the total-to-document drill path.
records.evidence_quote: You can branch from the line item report to the corresponding document.

records.claim_text: A project hierarchy report opens collapsed, showing only the top two levels, with an explicit expand-all action to reveal assigned orders and activities.
records.evidence_quote: The start list shows only the first two levels of the project hierarchy.

records.claim_text: A persistent navigation block offers every characteristic declared for the report, so the user re-pivots the same selected data set without re-querying.
records.evidence_quote: the system offers all the characteristics you specified when creating the report

records.claim_text: Clicking a column header swaps the drilldown axis (for example value category versus object), producing a transposed breakdown of the same data.
records.evidence_quote: the system switches the value category and object around, resulting in a different breakdown

records.claim_text: A single reset action restores the report to exactly the state it had when first executed, after arbitrary drilldown navigation.
records.evidence_quote: return to exactly the list displayed when you started the report

records.claim_text: A database profile determines which object types (WBS elements with hierarchy, networks, orders) enter the report selection, and is chosen at first report access.
records.evidence_quote: A database profile controls what objects (WBS elements, with hierarchy, networks, orders) are included in the selection.

records.claim_text: Cost element reports evaluate one or more projects in detail by cost element, and cover project definitions, WBS, networks, orders and valuated network materials.
records.evidence_quote: You can use cost element reports to evaluate one or more projects in detail by cost element.

records.claim_text: Cost element reports are authored with a Report Painter tool, so customers copy and adapt delivered reports rather than coding new ones.
records.evidence_quote: Cost element reports are created using the Report Painter, which means the Report Painter functions are available in your reports.

records.claim_text: In the delivered report 6PP1 the 'Total' column is actual plus commitment, and that total is explicitly described as all costs assigned.
records.evidence_quote: The total represents the actual and commitment costs added together; it therefore represents all the costs assigned.

records.claim_text: The delivered variance column is computed as actual minus plan, with a companion column expressing that variance as a percentage of planned costs.
records.evidence_quote: The figure in the absolute variance column is calculated by deducting the planned costs figure from the actual costs figure.

records.claim_text: A dedicated delivered report shows commitment values for a fiscal year broken down by period, i.e. commitment is a first-class periodised measure.
records.evidence_quote: Displays commitment values for a fiscal year, broken down by period

records.topic: Line items - actual and commitment always written
records.claim_text: Line items are always written for actual and commitment data with at least one line item per posting; plan line items are conditional.
records.evidence_quote: Line items are always documented for actual and commitment data. At least one line item is written for each posting.

records.claim_text: Plan line items are only written under specific conditions, so a plan-side drill to document is not universally available the way actual and commitment drill is.
records.evidence_quote: The system writes plan line items only under certain conditions.

records.claim_text: A commitment line item is created at the moment a commitment is set up, for example when a purchase order is raised against the project.
records.evidence_quote: Commitment line items are created as a commitment is set up - for example, for a purchase order.

records.claim_text: Budget changes are themselves documented as line items, so budget movement is auditable at document granularity alongside actual and commitment.
records.evidence_quote: The system uses line items to document budget changes which you save.

records.claim_text: From any project line item the user branches directly to the document display for deeper analysis; this is the terminal step of the drill path.
records.evidence_quote: You can analyze individual line items in more detail by branching directly to the document display.

records.claim_text: Line item reports are reachable both directly from the application transaction and from other reports, not only from a reports menu.
records.evidence_quote: You can access line item reports directly from the application or from other reports.

records.claim_text: Commitment line item reports carry an 'Open items only' restriction plus a posting-date timeframe; this is the native mechanism for isolating still-open commitments.
records.evidence_quote: Select the Open items only field if you want to restrict the display to items which are still open.

records.claim_text: Line item reports select on project, WBS element, network/order and activity, so the same report serves both summary and leaf-level enquiry.
records.evidence_quote: You can access line item reports for the following objects or object intervals:

records.topic: Cost element restriction on line items
records.claim_text: Line item selection can be narrowed by a single cost element, a cost element interval, or a cost element group.
records.evidence_quote: Enter a cost element, cost element interval, or cost element group.

records.claim_text: Budget line item selection asks for fiscal year and whether overall values are shown as well as annual values, reflecting the overall/annual budget duality.
records.evidence_quote: specify the fiscal year and whether you want to display the overall values as well as the annual values

records.claim_text: A saved display variant governs which columns appear in the line item list, and users may define their own in addition to delivered ones.
records.evidence_quote: The display variant controls which fields are displayed in the basic list

records.claim_text: Project line item reports can be run online, run and printed immediately, or scheduled to run in background - three explicit execution modes.
records.evidence_quote: To execute the line item report in the background, choose Report  Execute in background .

records.topic: Line item report with hierarchy tree
records.claim_text: The enhanced actual line item report renders the project hierarchy as a navigation tree beside the list, so users move between structure and detail in one screen.
records.evidence_quote: all project hierarchies are displayed in a navigation tree to the left of the screen

records.claim_text: The structure overview evaluates project structure flexibly by different criteria and is the structural counterpart to the value-oriented hierarchy report.
records.evidence_quote: You can use the structure overview to flexibly evaluate the structure of your project according to different criteria.

records.topic: Original document display from structure report
records.claim_text: The structure overview can display original documents for objects listed in the overview, extending drill-to-document beyond the financial reports.
records.evidence_quote: Display original documents for objects that appear in the overview

records.claim_text: The simplified project structure overview drops plan versions, project versions and customer-specific fields - a documented functional trade-off of the friendlier variant.
records.evidence_quote: Plan versions, project versions, and customer-specific fields are not supported in the project structure overview.

records.claim_text: The structures information system is positioned as the technical monitoring and control layer, distinct from the cost/revenue information system.
records.evidence_quote: The Information System for structures allows you to monitor and control your projects technically.

records.claim_text: Structure reporting evaluates not only current data but also simulation versions, project versions and archived projects, which a like-for-like replacement must account for.
records.evidence_quote: allows you to evaluate not only original data but also data from simulation and project versions and archived projects

records.topic: Hierarchy display - filters vs dynamic selections
records.claim_text: Filters only hide rows in the evaluation and never change database selection or shift hierarchy levels; dynamic selections change what is read.
records.evidence_quote: Filters have no effect on database selection, but temporarily hide elements in the evaluation.

records.claim_text: When dynamic selections exclude a WBS element the hierarchy collapses and the excluded element's costs are not rolled up - totals change with selection.
records.evidence_quote: The costs of the hidden WBS element are not rolled up.

records.claim_text: The project hierarchy is always shown complete; unauthorized objects appear with minimal data rather than being removed, preserving structural context.
records.evidence_quote: The project hierarchy is always displayed in its entirety. Objects for which you do not have authorization will be shown with only minimal data.

records.claim_text: Progress analysis exists to reveal project state and trend so corrective action can be taken when the project deviates from plan.
records.evidence_quote: You use progress analysis to obtain information on the state of your project and how it is developing.

records.claim_text: Because deliverables are planned in activities, project progress is determined at activity level and then aggregated up the work breakdown structure.
records.evidence_quote: In the Project System, deliverables are generally planned in activities. This means that project progress should be determined at activity level.

records.claim_text: The system derives BCWP and BCWS by applying the determined percentage of completion to a reference factor, typically planned costs or budget.
records.evidence_quote: Calculates the BCWP and BCWS based on the reference factor (planned costs, budget)

records.claim_text: Progress analysis only recognises costs that were planned by cost element; unstructured or non-cost-element plan values do not feed earned value.
records.evidence_quote: Note that progress analysis only considers costs planned by cost element.

records.claim_text: Official worked example shows a plan/actual comparison looking favourable while earned value analysis exposes both a cost variance and a schedule slip.
records.evidence_quote: In addition to the cost variance, the report shows that there is a time variance.

records.claim_text: Percentage of completion and earned value are exposed through three report types: structure-oriented progress reports, hierarchy drilldown reports, and Report Painter/Writer reports.
records.evidence_quote: The percentage of completion (POC) and earned value are important project key figures.

records.topic: POC not available in hierarchy reports
records.claim_text: Percentage of completion cannot be evaluated in the hierarchy drilldown reports; only the monetary earned value figures are available there.
records.evidence_quote: You cannot evaluate the POC in the hierarchy reports.

records.claim_text: The delivered progress analysis detail report contrasts aggregated against nonaggregated BCWS, BCWP, planned cost, actual cost, value variance, value index and work variance.
records.evidence_quote: This report compares the aggregated values with the nonaggregated values.

records.topic: No delivered Report Painter EVA reports
records.claim_text: No standard Report Painter reports for progress analysis are delivered; cost-element-level earned value reporting must be built by the customer.
records.evidence_quote: We do not supply any standard Report Painter reports for progress analysis purposes.

records.claim_text: Progress plan data is stored under value type P1 and actual under P2, with original values under activity PEV1 and adjusted values under PEV2.
records.evidence_quote: Planned data is recorded under value type P1 and actual data is recorded under value type P2.

records.topic: Progress report selection requires two versions
records.claim_text: A progress analysis report must be selected by both a plan version and a progress version, so version pairing is part of the report contract.
records.evidence_quote: The report must be selected by means of both the plan version and the progress version.

records.claim_text: From the hierarchical progress display the user navigates into a period breakdown and graphical displays for the selected project component.
records.evidence_quote: you can navigate to a project component in the period breakdown and the graphic displays

records.claim_text: A dedicated progress workbench displays POC, BCWS and BCWP per project object in one table with grid or tree display modes.
records.evidence_quote: you can check the percentage of completion (POC), the budgeted cost of work scheduled (BCWS), or the budgeted cost of work performed

records.claim_text: The progress workbench is not read-only: users confirm actual start/finish dates, update POC values and change system/user status directly from the report.
records.evidence_quote: Update POC values, user fields, and customer fields

records.claim_text: Double-clicking a row in the progress report opens the detail screen of that project object - row-to-master-record navigation is expected.
records.evidence_quote: Navigate to the detail screen for a project object by double-clicking the object

records.claim_text: Objects opened in the progress workbench are automatically locked for editing in the project editor and vice versa, preventing concurrent edits.
records.evidence_quote: All project objects that you call up in the progress analysis workbench are automatically locked for editing in the Project Builder, and vice versa.

records.claim_text: Estimated cost at completion is computed as actual plus commitment already incurred plus the updated cost to complete.
records.evidence_quote: The resulting figure is arrived at by adding the actual and commitment costs already incurred in the project to the updated cost to complete.

records.claim_text: Cost forecast results are written into a dedicated forecast version (standard version 110) so forecast, plan and actual coexist as separate value sets.
records.evidence_quote: The standard system offers forecast version 110.

records.claim_text: A delivered hierarchy report evaluates forecast values, cost to complete and estimated cost at completion together in one hierarchy.
records.evidence_quote: we deliver hierarchy report Forecast 12CTC1 so that you can evaluate forecast values, the cost to complete, and the estimated costs at completion.

records.claim_text: Commitment values dated before the forecast key date period are recorded in the forecast version as of the key date period, shifting their period attribution.
records.evidence_quote: Commitment values from periods before the period of the cost forecast key date are recorded in the forecast version as of the period

records.claim_text: A commitment identifies costs that will be incurred in the future for requested or ordered materials and services, reserving funds ahead of the actual posting.
records.evidence_quote: Identifies costs that will be incurred in the future for materials and services that you have requested or ordered.

records.claim_text: A project commitment is one whose initial account assignment is a project or a WBS element, distinguishing it from order and cost centre commitments.
records.evidence_quote: The commitment is initially assigned to a project, or to a work breakdown structure element.

records.claim_text: Project commitments arise from purchase requisitions, purchase orders and funds commitments, the last covering costs not yet tied to a specific procurement document.
records.evidence_quote: You can use Funds Commitments to reserve funds for costs you are fairly certain to incur, but you cannot yet assign to a specific business transaction

records.claim_text: For projects, availability control can check against either the current budget or the released budget, unlike internal orders which check current budget only.
records.evidence_quote: For projects, availability control can check against the current budget or the released budget.

records.claim_text: Current budget is not the original budget: it is original budget plus supplements, minus returns, adjusted by repostings from the budget.
records.evidence_quote: The current budget is made up of

records.claim_text: Availability control can be configured year-independent or year-dependent, and in controlling area currency or object currency, giving eight possible check bases.
records.evidence_quote: you can decide whether availability control is carried out on the basis of year-independent (= total values) or year-dependent values.

records.claim_text: Project summarization builds a separate summarization hierarchy from master data characteristics so projects can be analysed across the whole business, not only within one project tree.
records.evidence_quote: You use the summarized data from the project summarization for controlling purposes covering your whole business.

records.claim_text: Summarization supports exception rules that highlight hierarchy nodes with traffic lights, an exception-based management-by-deviation reporting pattern.
records.evidence_quote: you stipulate that the system highlights particular nodes in the hierarchy per the exception, using traffic lights.

records.claim_text: Summarization is delivered set to background processing because the run can take significant time; the info system then reports on the built hierarchy.
records.evidence_quote: We supply summarization set to background processing because the summarization run can take some time.

records.claim_text: A single info system profile bundles the database profile and field display settings used by the structure overview and individual overviews.
records.evidence_quote: The PS info system profile combines all the profiles you require for the structure overview and individual overviews

records.claim_text: The database profile also selects the data origin - operative data, version data, archive data or standard structures - as a report-time switch.
records.evidence_quote: You can specify which data the system should look for in the database or archive.

records.claim_text: A project-oriented procurement view consolidates purchase requisitions, purchase orders, order history, reservations and goods movements per project object in one configurable overview.
records.evidence_quote: Consolidating information from the procurement process from a variety of applications in a structured and individual overview

records.claim_text: Documents appear in the procurement overview only if assigned to a project object; requirements held in plant stock have no direct project link and are excluded.
records.evidence_quote: For a component or document to be displayed in ProMan it must be assigned to a project object, in general a WBS element or a network activity.

records.claim_text: The modern project procurement list shows delivered-versus-ordered quantity as an inline micro chart per purchase order, the practical substitute for a commitment ageing view.
records.evidence_quote: the quantity that is delivered as against the quantity that is ordered

records.claim_text: The current-generation project budget report compares budget against assigned value, where assigned value is defined as actual costs plus commitments.
records.evidence_quote: you can easily monitor project costs and budget by comparing budget with assigned value (actual costs and commitments)

records.topic: Budget report - drill to accounting document
records.claim_text: From the budget report the user navigates to the journal entries behind a document, preserving the total-to-source-document expectation in the modern UI.
records.evidence_quote: Navigate to view journal entries of a document

records.topic: Budget report - line item drill dimensions
records.claim_text: Line item costs can be drilled by fiscal year, fiscal period, company code and controlling area, with amounts shown in five parallel currencies.
records.evidence_quote: Drill down to view line item costs by fiscal year, fiscal period, company code

records.claim_text: The user sets the depth to which the project tree is expanded as an explicit report parameter rather than expanding node by node.
records.evidence_quote: Enter the level to which a project tree must be expanded

records.claim_text: Users select one or more projects or WBS elements in the summary grid then trigger a View Details action to reach budget and cost line items.
records.evidence_quote: choose View Details to navigate to view budget and costs at the line item level

records.topic: Budget relevance flag on line items
records.claim_text: Line items carry an explicit budget-relevant flag; where no availability control profile is active all costs show and are flagged not budget relevant.
records.evidence_quote: Such line items will have No as the value in the Budget Relevant Values column.

records.claim_text: The current-generation project cost report compares plan costs with actual costs and exposes variance plus commitments and baseline costs alongside.
records.evidence_quote: you can easily monitor project costs by comparing plan costs with actual costs

records.claim_text: Overall variance is shown in company code currency only when all selected projects and WBS elements share the same company code currency.
records.evidence_quote: Overall variance and costs such as planned cost, actual cost, commitment cost, and project stock cost are visible in company code currency only

records.topic: Hierarchy with or without assigned orders
records.claim_text: The cost report lets the user include or exclude assigned orders from the reported object hierarchy, changing what rolls into the project total.
records.evidence_quote: You can choose to view a hierarchy of objects by including or excluding orders.

records.claim_text: Project cost overviews ignore internal settlements and settlements within the project, counting only external sender settlements, to avoid double counting.
records.evidence_quote: Only the settlements from external senders are considered in the overview. All internal settlements or settlements from the project or from the assigned objects

records.claim_text: Planned project costs are read from a central financial planning table and actual costs from the universal journal entry table, two distinct stores.
records.evidence_quote: The planned costs are derived from the central financial planning table, ACDOCP; and the actual costs are derived from the table for universal journal entry

records.claim_text: The cost overview offers an aggregated view where WBS and assigned order costs roll up the project hierarchy, and a non-aggregated view at account assignment object level.
records.evidence_quote: Aggregated Cost View: The costs of WBS elements and the assigned orders are aggregated by the project hierarchy.

records.claim_text: In the aggregated view selecting a parent node auto-selects all nested nodes, whereas the non-aggregated view requires each object to be selected individually.
records.evidence_quote: selecting the parent WBS element automatically selects all the nested WBS elements

records.claim_text: Only cost postings whose GL account belongs to the selected GL account hierarchy are considered; postings to other accounts are silently excluded from the report.
records.evidence_quote: Only the cost postings related to G/L accounts, which are part of a G/L account hierarchy are considered within the report.

records.claim_text: A plan category distinguishes different sets of plan data and determines which object types have planned costs shown, and categories can be grouped virtually.
records.evidence_quote: The Plan Category is used to distinguish between different sets of plan data.

records.claim_text: A per-report switch decides whether a WBS filter returns only that element's line items or those of all child WBS elements and assigned objects too.
records.evidence_quote: the result displays the cost line items for the WBS elements, all child WBS elements

records.claim_text: Selecting a project object in the cost overview enables a details action that navigates to the line item application for further analysis.
records.evidence_quote: you can click on this button to navigate to the Project Cost Line Items app

records.claim_text: Vendor training presents financial project reporting as exactly three families - hierarchy reports, cost element reports and line item reports - each with a defined role.
records.evidence_quote: Line item reports: These enable you to evaluate line items and documents.

records.claim_text: Hierarchy reports drill down by various characteristics and can call line items and documents, making total-to-document the trained user's default expectation.
records.evidence_quote: Hierarchy reports allow you to drilldown based on various characteristics, and to call line items and documents.

records.claim_text: The structure information system evaluates structural and logistical aspects of a project while also displaying costs, revenues and other values inside the structure.
records.evidence_quote: The structure information system evaluates the structural and logistical aspects of projects and also displays costs, revenues, and other data in the structure.

records.claim_text: Structure reports support filters and exceptions that either select particular objects or highlight them in a different colour in place.
records.evidence_quote: define filters or exceptions to select particular objects or highlight these in a different color

records.claim_text: Trained users expect to create and change project structures and assigned orders directly from within reports, not only to read them.
records.evidence_quote: Display and change assigned orders, for example, production orders assigned to WBS elements.

records.claim_text: Project objects can be evaluated against alternative hierarchies such as the cost centre or profit centre hierarchy, not only the WBS hierarchy.
records.evidence_quote: you can evaluate your objects in accordance with your cost center or profit center hierarchy

records.claim_text: Percentage of completion is the ratio of activity performed up to a key date expressed as a percentage of total work for the activity or project.
records.evidence_quote: The percentage of completion (POC) describes the ratio of activity performed up to a key date as a percentage of the total work

records.claim_text: BCWS is the budgeted cost of work scheduled, i.e. costs according to planned progress at a given point in time.
records.evidence_quote: BCWS: budgeted cost of work scheduled (costs according to planned progress)

records.claim_text: BCWP is the budgeted cost of work performed, i.e. target costs according to actual progress achieved.
records.evidence_quote: BCWP: budgeted cost of work performed (target costs according to actual progress)

records.claim_text: Schedule deviation is determined by comparing BCWS with BCWP; a lower BCWP indicates the project is progressing more slowly than planned.
records.evidence_quote: By comparing BCWS with BCWP, you can determine any deviations from the schedule

records.claim_text: Cost variance is determined by comparing BCWP with actual costs (ACWP); actual above earned value means the project is running expensive.
records.evidence_quote: By comparing the BCWP with actual costs, you can determine any cost variances

records.topic: POC storage as statistical key figure
records.claim_text: Percentages of completion are stored as statistical key figures, which are themselves assigned to value categories for reporting.
records.evidence_quote: POCs are recorded under statistical key figures. For reporting purposes, statistical key figures are assigned to value categories.

records.claim_text: Nine POC measurement techniques exist including start/finish rule, estimation, milestone technique, time, cost, quantity and secondary proportionality, degree of processing and user exit.
records.evidence_quote: Degree of processing (only for activities, only for actual POCs)

records.claim_text: A measurement method pairs a technique with parameters such as a start POC, producing named variants like the 0-100 method and the 20-80 method.
records.evidence_quote: 0-100 method, with a start POC of zero

records.claim_text: With the estimation technique a maximum POC caps actual progress until the activity is finished, guarding against overvaluing nearly complete work; 80% is the recommended cap.
records.evidence_quote: In the case of estimation, we recommend a maximum POC of 80%.

records.claim_text: Progress values are aggregated up the project structure using weighting factors, with the project cost plan being the recommended weighting factor.
records.evidence_quote: The system uses specific weighting factors to summarize progress values in the project structure.

records.topic: EVA stored in its own plan version
records.claim_text: Earned value analysis results are stored in a separate plan version and evaluated from either the structure information system or the controlling information system.
records.evidence_quote: You can store earned value analysis in a separate plan version and evaluate it using the structure information system

records.claim_text: Assigned funds are commitments plus actual costs plus the planned costs of apportioned orders, and are the quantity availability control checks against budget.
records.evidence_quote: Together with the planned costs of apportioned orders, these forms of fund commitments result in what are referred to as assigned funds.

records.claim_text: The funds overview report is characterised as passive availability control - the same budget-versus-assigned comparison presented for reading rather than blocking.
records.evidence_quote: The funds overview can be regarded as a passive availability control.

records.claim_text: Availability control first resolves the budget-bearing WBS elements, then aggregates assigned funds from that element and its lower-level assignable elements before checking.
records.evidence_quote: The assigned funds are checked against the budgets of the controlling elements.

records.claim_text: A WBS element's budget must be greater than or equal to the aggregated budgets of the WBS elements directly assigned below it.
records.evidence_quote: the budget of a WBS element must be greater than or equal to the aggregated budgets of the lower-level WBS element assigned directly to it

records.claim_text: Budget checking uses distributed/distributable views for structural consistency and cumulative/remaining views for consistency of annual values against the overall total.
records.evidence_quote: You can use the cumulative or remaining views to check the distribution of the budget over a fiscal year.

records.claim_text: Budget is the approved and binding cost framework, distinct from the cost plan which precedes it and forms the basis for proposing and approving that budget.
records.evidence_quote: The budget is the approved cost framework for a project. It differs from the cost plan in that it is binding.

records.claim_text: Once the original budget is locked by user status it can only be changed through supplements, returns and transfers, each of which is documented.
records.evidence_quote: If you lock (freeze) the original budget in this way, you can only change it by defining supplements, returns, and transfers.

records.topic: Open commitment ageing - no native report found
records.claim_text: No first-party documentation of a standard project open-commitment ageing report was found; open commitments are isolated instead via the open-items-only line item filter and posting-date ranges.
records.evidence_quote: In the case of commitment line item reports, enter the date or timeframe in which the line items are to be selected.

records.claim_text: The trained user's expected drill chain is hierarchy total to characteristic breakdown to cost element to line item to source document, with each hop documented separately.
records.evidence_quote: Use the Goto menu to access further hierarchy, cost element, and line item reports.

records.topic: Drilldown in line item reports - support note only
records.claim_text: The dedicated support page on drilldown in line item reports carries no substantive prose, only pointers to SAP Notes 107605 and 161543 about object selection and the include-hierarchy flag.
records.evidence_quote: flag 'Incl. hierarchy'  is explained in notes 107605 and 161543.

gaps: No first-party evidence found for a standard SAP PS 'open commitment ageing' report with ageing buckets. Searched help.sap.com (three query shapes) and general web on 2026-08-05. Nearest documented mechanisms: commitment line item report with 'Open items only' plus posting-date timeframe, and the project procurement list with delivered-vs-ordered micro charts. Treat commitment ageing as NEW functionality for the target build, not a like-for-like port.

The 'List of SAP Project System Reports' support page (help.sap.com/docs/SUPPORT_CONTENT/prosys/3363505772.html) was not rendered; only its sibling stub page was. A full transaction-code inventory (CJI3/CJI5/CJE0/S_ALR_*) is therefore NOT evidenced in this lane - every transaction code seen was in community sources only and has been deliberately omitted.
The 'Fiori Apps in Project System' index page renders with a title but no body, so no evidenced app inventory for on-premise PS.

'Project Cost Line Items' detail sections (Key Features, Data Selection and Filtering, Functions for Analysing Costs) are lazy-loaded accordions that did not expand under the browser tool; only the intro paragraph is evidenced. The learning.sap.com Reporting lesson was used to cover the same ground at Tier 2.

No page was found describing a delivered ACWP column by that name; actual cost is the evidenced term used in place of ACWP throughout SAP PS documentation. Do not label a column ACWP on the strength of this lane.

'Hierarchy Setup and the Effect on Values Displayed' was referenced from the hierarchy report page but its GUID was not located; the related 'Project Hierarchy Display' page was fetched instead and covers roll-up/filter semantics.

Availability control tolerance-limit specifics (usage percentages, three system reactions) are evidenced only at Tier 2 from the budgeting lesson and from a search snippet; the Tier-1 tolerance-limit page was not fetched. Any tolerance threshold numbers must be re-verified before being written into a spec.
